core_obligations: The K-injective representative (proof lines 2617-2620): a K-injective complex with injective terms is chosen to represent the object E, using the cited embedding theorem.

Representing the system by complexes (proof lines 2621-2634): complexes representing the terms of the inverse system are chosen inductively, with maps representing the transition maps in both directions, the negative direction being chosen termwise injective.

Lifting homotopies (proof lines 2634-2652): the author shows that the representing maps can be chosen compatibly, by choosing an arbitrary representing map and correcting it with a lifted homotopy, the lift existing because the terms of the K-injective complex are injective and the map to be lifted over is termwise injective.

The acyclic replacements (proof lines 2654-2672): termwise injective maps into acyclic K-injective complexes with injective terms are produced by mapping to the cone on the identity and applying the embedding theorem, and the transition maps are extended to these replacements by the same lifting argument.

The filtered complex (proof lines 2674-2701): the big diagram built out of products of the acyclic replacements and the object I is shown termwise injective, the verification of injectivity of its arrows being left to the reader with that sentence written out, and because products in the derived category are products of K-injective complexes and the replacements are acyclic, the diagram represents the given system, which is the conclusion.
proof_roadmap: Choose a K-injective representative of the object and representatives of the terms of the system.
Make the representatives compatible by lifting homotopies along termwise injective maps into complexes with injective terms.
Replace the representatives by acyclic K-injective ones and extend the transition maps.
Assemble the product diagram and use the product rule in the derived category to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that an inverse system of objects of the derived category of a Grothendieck abelian category mapping compatibly to a fixed object is realised by a filtered complex whose filtration steps represent the terms of the system (statement lines 2601-2615). The proof is a complete argument: a K-injective representative with injective terms is chosen (proof lines 2617-2620), the terms of the system are represented by complexes in both directions (proof lines 2621-2634), the representing maps are made compatible by correcting them with lifted homotopies, which is where injectivity of the terms is used (proof lines 2634-2652), acyclic K-injective replacements are built by mapping to the cone on the identity (proof lines 2654-2672), and the product diagram is shown to represent the given system using the product rule for K-injective complexes (proof lines 2674-2701). The non-formal content is the homotopy lifting and the assembly of the product diagram. The claim is H3.
